failure: free-sliding puck under-travel: model predicts 0.208 m vs real 0.265 m (bias -0.057 m); worst at gripper-far/high-travel (0.116 m); scales with puck speed

hypotheses.statement: The learned dynamics over-estimate the puck's deceleration (too much friction/damping), so the imagined puck stops earlier than the real one.
supporting_evidence: signed travel bias is negative in BOTH baseline (-0.071) and rollout (-0.057)
contradicting_evidence: rollout training (longer objective) reduced the bias, so part of it is horizon-related
hypotheses.predicted_consequence: predicted per-step object speed decays faster than real even at short horizon; a better velocity input would NOT fix it
hypotheses.result: one-step speed ratio 0.967 (>0.9): no strong one-step over-damping, so a one-step friction bias is NOT supported; a residual multi-step over-damping cannot be ruled out

hypotheses.statement: The input lacks an adequate ABSOLUTE object-velocity signal: object_velp (cols 14:17) is stored relative to the gripper, so once the gripper decelerates/leaves the model cannot represent the puck's remaining momentum and defaults to stopping.
motivating_observations: object_velp verified gripper-relative in Phase 9A (only z-axis correlates with raw displacement)
failure concentrated where gripper is FAR (0.116 m) -- exactly where relative != absolute velocity
supporting_evidence: regime is high-uncertainty not high-OOD (rho 0.66 vs 0.22) -> representation not coverage
contradicting_evidence: not yet tested directly; awaits E_abs_velocity_feature
hypotheses.predicted_consequence: adding an absolute object-velocity feature substantially reduces the free-slide under-travel bias
hypotheses.result: gripper is already far at free-slide start (0.144 m) and keeps receding; one-step ok but the speed gap opens as the model propagates its own state -> consistent with a velocity-representation gap. Decisive test: E_abs_velocity_feature (pending)

hypotheses.statement: Fast free-sliding states are under-represented in the training data, so the model extrapolates them toward 'stopped'.
motivating_observations: free-slide is the minority regime (24% of windows)
contradicting_evidence: OOD ranks error only weakly (Spearman 0.215) and free-slide windows are NOT strongly out-of-distribution -- evidence AGAINST coverage as the primary cause
hypotheses.predicted_consequence: adding verified free-slide real data reduces the bias; bias concentrated in high-OOD windows
hypotheses.result: OOD->error weak (0.215) argues against coverage; awaits E_add_freeslide_data

hypotheses.statement: The failure is purely a multi-step propagation artifact of the training objective's horizon; the one-step dynamics are fine.
motivating_observations: rollout training (K>1) reduced the bias from -0.071 to -0.057
supporting_evidence: bias decreased when the objective horizon increased (baseline->rollout)
contradicting_evidence: bias persists at -0.057 even with rollout training -- a residual remains
hypotheses.predicted_consequence: one-step predicted object speed is ~correct; the gap opens only with rollout depth and vanishes as K->full
hypotheses.result: speed gap grows with horizon (one-step 0.967 -> late 0.795); consistent, BUT the travel bias persisted (-0.057) under rollout training, so horizon alone is incomplete

experiments.name: E_speed_decay
experiments.description: predicted vs real per-step object speed on held-out free-slide windows

predicted_outcome.H_friction: pred speed below real from the FIRST step (one-step over-damping)
predicted_outcome.H_velocity: one-step may be low when gripper co-moves; gap widens after gripper leaves
predicted_outcome.H_horizon: one-step speed ~correct; gap appears only with rollout depth

result.conclusion: over-damping is a multi-step effect, not one-step; live contenders are H_velocity and H_horizon, to be separated by E_abs_velocity_feature in Phase 9E/9G; strong one-step friction (H_friction) unsupported

predicted_outcome.H_horizon: bias approaches zero as K grows (large, monotone)
